claim: Vision and action share mechanisms that encode numbers.

claim: Animals estimate spontaneously and reasonably accurately the approximate quantity of arrays of objects, without recourse to other forms of representation, such as density.
source: Animals, including humans, estimate spontaneously and reasonably accurately the approximate quantity of arrays of objects, without recourse to other forms of representation, such as density (Cicchini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Newborn infants of less than 3 days show selective habituation to number.
source: Even newborn infants of less than 3 days show selective habituation to number (Izard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Number is encoded by intraparietal and prefrontal cortex in human primates.
source: There is now very good evidence in both human and non-human primates that number is encoded by intraparietal and prefrontal cortex (Castelli et al., 2006; Dehaene et al., 2003; Harvey et al., 2013; Nieder, 2005, 2012, 2016; Nieder et al., 2006; Nieder and Miller, 2004; Piazza and Eger, 2016; Piazza et al., 2004, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Number is encoded by intraparietal and prefrontal cortex in non-human primates.
source: There is now very good evidence in both human and non-human primates that number is encoded by intraparietal and prefrontal cortex (Castelli et al., 2006; Dehaene et al., 2003; Harvey et al., 2013; Nieder, 2005, 2012, 2016; Nieder et al., 2006; Nieder and Miller, 2004; Piazza and Eger, 2016; Piazza et al., 2004, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Number is encoded by intraparietal and prefrontal cortex even in numerically naive monkeys.
source: even in numerically naive monkeys (Viswanathan and Nieder, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: There exists a visual sense of number within a parietal–frontal network.
source: All these studies point to the existence of a visual sense of number within a parietal–frontal network (Dehaene, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A truly abstract sense of number should be capable of encoding the numerosity of any set of discrete elements, displayed simultaneously or sequentially, in whatever sensory modality.
source: A truly abstract sense of number should be capable of encoding the numerosity of any set of discrete elements, displayed simultaneously or sequentially, in whatever sensory modality.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about what would constitute an abstract number sense.

claim: Neurons in the lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC) of behaving monkeys encode numerosity for both auditory and visual sensory modalities.
source: Neurons in the lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC) of behaving monkeys encode numerosity for both auditory and visual sensory modalities, suggesting supra-modal numerosity processing (Nieder, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Neurons in the lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC) of behaving monkeys suggest supra-modal numerosity processing.
source: Neurons in the lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC) of behaving monkeys encode numerosity for both auditory and visual sensory modalities, suggesting supra-modal numerosity processing (Nieder, 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Separate populations of neurons in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) respond selectively to sequential or simultaneous numerical displays.
source: Another study reported separate populations of neurons in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) responding selectively to sequential or simultaneous numerical displays, while a third set of neurons showed numerosity selectivity for both simultaneous and sequential presentations, suggesting that the information about spatial and temporal numerosity converges to a more abstract representation (Nieder et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A third set of neurons in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) showed numerosity selectivity for both simultaneous and sequential presentations.
source: Another study reported separate populations of neurons in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) responding selectively to sequential or simultaneous numerical displays, while a third set of neurons showed numerosity selectivity for both simultaneous and sequential presentations, suggesting that the information about spatial and temporal numerosity converges to a more abstract representation (Nieder et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The information about spatial and temporal numerosity converges to a more abstract representation in the intraparietal sulcus.
source: Another study reported separate populations of neurons in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) responding selectively to sequential or simultaneous numerical displays, while a third set of neurons showed numerosity selectivity for both simultaneous and sequential presentations, suggesting that the information about spatial and temporal numerosity converges to a more abstract representation (Nieder et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A right lateralized fronto-parietal circuit is activated by both auditory and visual number sequences.
source: There is also evidence from functional imaging in humans for a right lateralized fronto-parietal circuit activated by both auditory and visual number sequences, and that right IPS is involved in processing both sequential and simultaneous numerosity formats (Castelli et al., 2006; Piazza et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Right IPS is involved in processing both sequential and simultaneous numerosity formats.
source: There is also evidence from functional imaging in humans for a right lateralized fronto-parietal circuit activated by both auditory and visual number sequences, and that right IPS is involved in processing both sequential and simultaneous numerosity formats (Castelli et al., 2006; Piazza et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Human adults are very efficient in making cross-modal and cross-format judgments, with very little cost in either accuracy or reaction times when comparing auditory with visual temporal sequences or dot arrays.
source: For example, human adults are very efficient in making cross-modal and cross-format judgments, with very little cost in either accuracy or reaction times when comparing auditory with visual temporal sequences or dot arrays (Barth et al., 2003; Brannon, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Pre-schoolers show similar accuracy for comparing spatial array of dots either with other spatial arrays, or with sequences of sounds.
source: Developmental work also show similar accuracy in pre-schoolers for comparing spatial array of dots either with other spatial arrays, or with sequences of sounds (Barth et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Infants prefer to look at screens displaying adults faces numerically matched with the soundtrack of adult voices.

claim: Adaptation is one of the more powerful psychophysical techniques to probe mechanisms.

claim: Number is highly susceptible to adaptation.

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Visually inspecting for a few seconds a large number of items results in the perceived numerosity of a subsequent ensemble to be strongly underestimated.
source: visually inspecting for a few seconds a large number of items results in the perceived numerosity of a subsequent ensemble to be strongly underestimated, and vice-versa after adaptation to low numbers (Burr and Ross, 2008).

claim: After adaptation to low numbers, the perceived numerosity of a subsequent ensemble is overestimated.
